exercises.tip: "باچر" (or "باجر") is the Gulf "tomorrow"; in the Emirates "يي" is also heard for "comes".

exercises.prompt: Complete: "أبي أروح البلد _____." Meaning: I want to go to the Old City.

too_formal.feedback: This is a more literary word for "old"; everyday Gulf speech says "القديم".

exercises.tip: Say "القديم" for old; in the Gulf "ق" is often pronounced like a hard "g".

exercises.prompt: Translate: "Bus."

too_formal.feedback: This is the standard written word for bus; spoken Gulf Arabic uses the loanword "باص".

exercises.tip: "تاكسي" and "باص" are both borrowed words.

exercises.prompt: Translate: "Will you drop me at the station?" (to a man)

too_formal.item: هل تستطيع أن توصلني إلى المحطة؟
too_formal.feedback: This is formal Arabic; the everyday question is just "توصلني...؟".

exercises.tip: Say the verb with a rising voice; no extra question word is needed.

challenge.title: Getting Around Dubai
challenge.instructions: Write and act out a conversation of at least 10 lines about getting to a meeting place across town. It must include calling or boarding a taxi or bus, asking the fare, asking for directions to a specific place, naming at least two places in town, and thanking the driver or the person who helped you. Use at least 8 target phrases from Unit 5 and include both a masculine-address and a feminine-address form.
required_elements: A request to a driver using أبي أروح or a similar phrase.
A question about the fare using كم.
At least one turn instruction using لف or دغري.
At least two named places, for example السوق, المسجد, البنك, or المحطة.
A thank-you exchange using مشكور وايد or الله يعطيك العافية.
One masculine-address form and one feminine-address form, for example اركب and اركبي.

dialogue.speaker: مريم
dialogue.arabic: السلام عليكم، لو سمحت، أبي أروح سوق الذهب.
dialogue.transliteration: as-salaamu 3alaykum, law samaht, abi arooh soog edh-dhahab.
dialogue.english: Peace be upon you, please, I want to go to the Gold Souk.

dialogue.speaker: سواق
dialogue.english: And upon you peace, get in (to a woman).

dialogue.speaker: مريم
dialogue.english: About how much is the fare?

dialogue.speaker: سواق
dialogue.english: About twenty dirhams.

dialogue.speaker: مريم
dialogue.arabic: زين. وين أقرب صيدلية من سوق الذهب؟
dialogue.transliteration: zeen. wayn agrab saydaliyya min soog edh-dhahab?
dialogue.english: Fine. Where is the nearest pharmacy from the Gold Souk?

dialogue.speaker: سواق
dialogue.arabic: قريبة، لف شمال بعد المسجد وتلقينها على يمينج.
dialogue.transliteration: gareeba, liff shimaal ba3d el-masjid w-tilgeenha 3ala yameenich.
dialogue.english: Near, turn left after the mosque and you'll find it on your right.

dialogue.speaker: مريم
dialogue.english: Thanks, stop here please.

dialogue.speaker: سواق
dialogue.english: There you go (to a woman), we arrived.

dialogue.speaker: مريم
dialogue.english: How much do I owe?

dialogue.speaker: سواق
dialogue.english: Just twenty dirhams.

dialogue.speaker: مريم
dialogue.arabic: تفضّل، والباقي لك. الله يعطيك العافية.
dialogue.transliteration: tfaddal, w-el-baagi lak. allah y3teek el-3aafya.
dialogue.english: Here, keep the change. Thank you.

dialogue.speaker: سواق
dialogue.english: God give you wellbeing, goodbye.
